note: A first input byte different from 0xff selects unversioned ZMTP/1.0 and preserves the already-read byte for the v1 decoder.
The selected protocol creates a v1 decoder that uses decoder_base_t with the default c_single_allocator static buffer policy.
After each socket read the decoder allocator is resized to the number of bytes just received, even when the decoder is backed by a fixed static allocation.
The read size is propagated into the allocator policy through the generic decoder resize hook.
The static allocator changes only its recorded buffer size, not the malloc allocation, so later reads can be scheduled using a size unrelated to the actual fixed buffer capacity.
The corrupted allocator size is later exposed as the amount of data the transport may read into the same static buffer.
